title: What Bridge Cities Is
definition: Bridge Cities: cities living on and around inhabited bridges.
description:
Bridge Cities — Signature Edition: cities living on and around inhabited bridges. This is the JAH-original vision, designed from first principles and labeled as Signature speculation throughout.

The Signature bridge hulls program starts where public roadmaps stop. Where public research asks what is fundable, the Signature line asks what is buildable: span districts rethought, bridge transit rebuilt, toll commons reimagined for the century ahead. Nothing here is presented as established fact — it is a designed future, fully specified.

This edition mirrors the public database record for record — concept, components, milestones, demos, drills, alliance, roadmap — but every entry is the Signature take: bolder timelines, integrated systems thinking, and the arch blocks ambition that defines the Signature line.

title: The Signature Vision: Bridge Cities
definition: The JAH-original Signature vision of Bridge Cities.
description:
The Signature vision of Bridge Cities does not ask what committees will fund — it asks what physics allows and what engineering can compound.

Signature bridge hulls program, charter one: master span districts at laboratory scale within the decade. Charter two: scale bridge transit manufacturing until cost collapses. Charter three: operate toll commons systems continuously, learning in public, improving every cycle.

This is a Signature concept — original JAH speculation, fully specified and honestly labeled. The public edition of this database carries the documented research record; this edition carries the bolder integrated vision: what Bridge Cities becomes when every piece is designed to work with every other piece from day one.

title: The bridge hulls Grid
definition: The bridge hulls Grid: a load-bearing component of Bridge Cities.
description:
The urban backbone: power, water, data and logistics woven into one span districts grid that the bridge hulls district runs on.

In the Bridge Cities architecture, the bridge hulls grid is load-bearing: without it the bridge hulls fails outright — Bridge Cities stops being Bridge Cities at all. Builders sequence this piece early because every other component assumes it works. In the Signature architecture this piece is designed first-class, not bolted on.

Maturity varies: some deployments of this piece exist today in simpler forms, while the full Bridge Cities-grade version remains a research target. The readiness estimator in this database scores it honestly.

t: 2030 — The first bridge hulls district opens at 50
title: 2030 — The first bridge hulls district opens at 50
definition: 2030 milestone on the Bridge Cities roadmap.
description:
The first bridge hulls district opens at 50,000 residents, its span districts grid and bridge transit mobility running at full design load.

What must be true first: the span districts results have to replicate outside the lab, bridge transit manufacturing must reach pilot scale, and toll commons operations need a year of continuous runtime. Miss any one and the date slips — that is the honest mechanics of forecasting. The Signature timeline pulls this earlier by integrating the pieces from day one.

Signals to watch: peer-reviewed span districts demonstrations, bridge transit cost curves bending down, and operators — not vendors — reporting toll commons uptime. When all three flash green, 2030 stops being a forecast and starts being a schedule. (4 years from the 2026 baseline.)

Depends on: span districts, bridge transit, toll commons.

title: Readiness Estimator: Bridge Cities
definition: Estimates Bridge Cities readiness from component maturity.
description:
The estimator scores the six Bridge Cities components on the TRL 1–9 scale and averages them into a verdict: research phase, pilot phase, or deployment phase. Scores derive from the component records in this database — change a component's maturity and the verdict moves.

Honest scoring is the point: a bridge hulls that averages TRL 3 is not failing, it is three phases from deployment, and the estimator tells you which component drags the average down. Fund that one first.

title: Bridge Cities Systems Simulator
definition: Simulates Bridge Cities operating for a day.
description:
The simulator walks a Bridge Cities installation through six operating steps, with seeded randomness standing in for real-world variation. Seed 73991 reproduces this exact run — change the seed in the program to explore other days.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where span districts monitoring, bridge transit redundancy, or toll commons maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: Bridge Cities Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Bridge Cities: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Bridge Cities — cities living on and around inhabited bridges.

Phase 1 — Prove (span districts): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (bridge transit): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (toll commons): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (arch blocks): bridge hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and river crossings-scale deployment begins.

Signature edition: phases overlap aggressively — integration starts on day one. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.

Each phase has exit criteria.
Unites all 20 records.
